content: 1. Epinephrine (racemic) and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Erdafitinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, separate the administration of P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index by at least 6 hours before or after erythromycin lactobionate. 4. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Eribulin and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If concurrent use is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 6. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 9. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of estradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. However, it decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of estradiol, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitor closely. 10. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of estrogens (conjugated synthetic) by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. However, it decreases estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of eszopiclone by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption and inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of eszopiclone to 1 mg/day. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 13. Ethanol decreases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 15. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of etoposide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of exemestane by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Erythromycin lactobionate and ezogabine both increase the risk of QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to prolong the QT interval. 22. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of felodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 25. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
